surface_mechanism_description: The growth on glass begins with the formation of an amorphous layer, and then there appears a coarsely grained structure containing anatase. In further growth, the crystallinity of this structure grows with the film thickness. The growth process on silicon begins with the appearance of fine crystals, which increase in size via fusion.
evidence: The authors of varied the concentration of hydroxy groups on the silicon surface by their partial replacement with hydride groups, with the surface hydrophobicity thereby raised, and analyzed changes in the structure of the forming titanium oxide films. In the end, they came to a conclusion that mostly single hydroxy groups are present on a hydrophobic silicon surface and reaction (1) occurs to give finer crystallites (as in the case shown in Figs. 2e and 5); on a hydrophilic surface, the concentration of hydroxy groups is higher and the synthesis occurs predominantly by reaction (2) to give coarser crystallites (as in Figs. 2a and 2c):
